method.label: Subtract the subsets with no primes

annotationRationale: Complement counting removes the prime-free subsets. The multiplication principle counts subsets through include-or-exclude choices, using subset and prime-number concepts.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution, subtracting the subsets of the four nonprime elements from all subsets; explains the powers-of-two counts.

review.mathCheck: There are 2⁸ subsets altogether. A prime-free subset uses only 4, 6, 8, and 9, giving 2⁴ subsets. Subtraction yields 256−16=240, choice D; the empty subset is correctly removed.
review.sourceMethodCheck: An originally worded, faithful adaptation of MAA solution #5's first approach on printed page 3. The candidate additionally explains the include-or-exclude basis of the subset counts.
review.annotationCheck: The key is correct. Prime classification, the complementary cases, and treatment of the empty set are explicit and sufficient.

nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower 4.OA.B.4 link supports background prime/composite classification within 2 through 9; factor-pair and multiple tasks are not demonstrated. No US links are supplied for complement counting, the multiplication principle, or subsets.
